source.title: Learning Distinct Features Helps, Provably
source.authors: Firas Laakom; Jenni Raitoharju; Alexandros Iosifidis; M. Gabbouj

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study measures feature diversity and reports its empirical association with the generalization gap, using a different measure and theoretical analysis. It does not test the specific versions V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper's reported empirical results concern feature diversity, not the memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch size, explicit regularization, magnitude-aware sharpness, or example-removal effects in V1–V8. Figure 2 gives correlation values in its caption and discussion; exact plotted gap values are not stated in the text. Theoretical bounds are arguments, not measured test-error outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study derives feature-diversity bounds and measures diversity during training and its association with the generalization gap. None of these results tests V1–V8. In particular, feature diversity is not magnitude-aware sharpness, and varying widths without reporting interpolation thresholds or test-error trends does not test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors derive bounds that decrease with their feature-diversity lower bound under stated assumptions, extending the analysis to additional losses and architectures. They report strong MNIST correlations between a diversity-based term and the generalization gap, increasing diversity during residual-network training, and increasing diversity with depth in MNIST fully connected networks. SGD implicitly optimizing diversity is presented as a conjecture.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies feature diversity and derives generalization bounds; its empirical measurements track diversity and its association with the gap, rather than testing the interventions or measures in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The Figure 2 correlation values vary with hidden-layer size: 128, 256, and 512 units have reported correlations 0.9948, 0.9939, and 0.9953, respectively. The text says increasing depth consistently increases feature diversity for the three tested fully connected model widths.

fits_no_version.finding: The diversity-based term has reported correlations of 0.9948, 0.9939, and 0.9953 with the MNIST generalization gap across training-set sizes for hidden widths 128, 256, and 512.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A diversity-based theoretical term tracks the generalization gap across training-set sizes in the tested MNIST networks; this association does not establish a causal diversity effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Last-hidden-layer feature diversity increases during the reported CIFAR-10 and ImageNet training experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature diversity increases during SGD training in the tested residual-network settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Final feature diversity increases with depth from 1 to 12 in MNIST fully connected ReLU networks of widths 256, 512, and 1024.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater depth produces higher final feature diversity in the tested MNIST fully connected networks.

record.peer_reviewed: ECML/PKDD; the supplied text labels the work a preprint
record.problems: The empirical diversity-gap comparison is shown for MNIST and three hidden sizes; exact plotted gap values are not stated. The reported correlations do not establish causation. The paper does not empirically test its generalization bounds across the broader settings discussed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test-error trends beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its dependence on data size, configuration, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; the reported diversity observations themselves are present. Figure 2 rescales the theoretical term to the gap's range, and both quantities vary with training-set size. The correlations therefore do not isolate diversity's contribution to generalization.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width passes the interpolation threshold.
Large-batch generalization under epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Effects of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: neural networks with intermediate layer size 128
rows.operation_detail: Compared the generalization gap with a theoretical term based on the diversity lower bound across training-set sizes.

conditions.value: 100 epochs; SGD; learning rate 0.1; batch size 256

rows.measure: Correlation between the theoretical term and generalization gap
rows.note: The text says results are averaged over 5 random seeds. It describes the plotted gap as test error minus train error in the caption, but later as test error minus train error in the setup and calls it generalization error; exact plotted gap values are not stated.
rows.check: The reported correlation of 0.9948 concerns a diversity-based term, not any claim version. The note misreports Figure 2's caption: it defines the gap as train error minus test error, whereas Section 5 defines it as test error minus train error. The sign is internally inconsistent.

rows.subject: three different ResNet models
rows.operation_detail: Tracked last-hidden-layer feature diversity during training.
rows.value: Diversity consistently increases during training for all three models.
rows.note: The text does not name the three ResNet models in this experiment.
rows.check: Increasing feature diversity during CIFAR-10 training is reported, but this measure cannot establish any V1–V8 effect.

rows.subject: ResNet50, ResNet101, ResNext50, and WideResNet50
rows.size_stated: ResNet50 and WideResNet50: 50 layers; ResNet101: 101 layers; ResNext50: 50 layers
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD using standard training protocol
rows.operation_detail: Tracked last-intermediate-layer feature diversity during training.
rows.value: SGD without explicit regularization implicitly optimizes diversity and converges toward regions with high feature distinctness.
rows.locator: Discussion, Figure 3 (a) and (b) and accompanying text
rows.note: The text states this as an observation and conjecture; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The measured result is increasing feature diversity during ImageNet training. SGD implicitly optimizing diversity is the authors' interpretation and Conjecture 1, rather than an established optimization mechanism. No adaptive-optimizer comparison or other V1–V8 outcome is measured.

rows.subject: FCN-256, FCN-512, and FCN-1024
rows.operation_detail: Measured final last-hidden-layer diversity across network depths.
rows.value: Increasing depth consistently leads to learning more distinct features and higher diversity for the different models.
rows.note: The text reports averages over 5 random seeds; exact plotted values are not stated. It also says that having more parameters does not always lead to higher diversity.
rows.check: The depth experiment measures final feature diversity, not held-out error or generalization past the interpolation threshold. It cannot establish V2 or another listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
